items.title: Kerala HC orders clearance of trash along highway till Kalamassery; will inspect Brahmapuram waste plant
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday ordered clearance of waste from identified dumping hotspot in Kochi [Suo Motu v State of Kerala] A Division Bench of Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas and Justice P Gopinath directed the State government to instruct panchayats and municipalities, through which the National Highway 966 passes till Kalamassery municipality, to clear accumulated waste from either side of the road. Pertinently, the Court said that it will be visiting the Brahmapuram waste treatment facility for a physical inspection on September 11 to verify whether it is functioning effectively. The Court said the waste dumped on roads belongs to the government or civil authorities and emphasised their duty to keep public places clean. The Court passed the order in a suo motu case initiated by the High Court to address the issue of waste management in the city. Justice P Gopinath and Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas Justice Thomas expressed concern over continued dumping of waste at various locations in Kochi. items.title: Why 4 in 10 Indian children go to private schools
items.summary: Four in 10 Indian schoolchildren were enrolled in private unaided schools in 2025-26, up from 35.4 percent in 2018-19, according to Unified District Information System for Education ( UDISE+ ) data. Private-school enrolment increased by about 3 million in the past year, while government schools—where 48 percent of children are enrolled—saw their numbers decline by about 2.7 million. In 12 states and two Union territories (UTs), more than half the students went to private schools. Bihar, Goa and Jharkhand had less than 20 percent enrolment in private schools, while West Bengal had under 10 percent. Parents are increasingly choosing private schools at lower levels: 71 percent students in pre-primary or kindergarten and 40 percent in primary (grades I to V) were in private schools. In contrast, about 10 percent of students at the primary level were in government schools. Research studies show, and experts say, that perceptions of learning, affordability, school performance and availability of English-medium instruction affect parents’ choices. Choosing a private school also comes at a higher cost. Average annual education-related expenditure was Rs 28,693 per student in private school

items.title: Protect interests of students: Supreme Court asks CBSE to address OSM evaluation issues
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to explore ways to protect the interests of students facing difficulties in entrance-based admissions due to their scores under the Board’s new On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluating answer sheets. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told that some students had cleared their CBSE examinations and had subsequently appeared for entrance examinations for other courses. However, they had not secured the minimum marks required for admission because of their CBSE scores, and some of the courses had already commenced. The plea linked the lesser marks/ scores to the irregularities in OSM evaluation system. The Bench then asked CBSE to examine the issue and find out how the interests of such students could be protected. "Please find out how can you protect their interest," the Court said before adjourning the matter. items.title: Delhi HC asks Centre, CBFC, film producers to decide on adding accessibility features in cinema, OTT for disabled
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed the Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), Central Board Of Film Certification (CBFC), Mythri Movie Makers and other relevant stakeholders to deliberate upon adding accessibility features in films released in cinema and over-the-top (OTT) platforms for disabled audience [ Rahul Bajaj vs. Mythri Movie Makers And Ors ]. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma passed the directions on August 10 while hearing a petition filed by disability rights activist and lawyer Rahul Bajaj. "This Court considers it appropriate to afford an opportunity to all concerned stakeholders to deliberate upon the issue and explore a mutually acceptable resolution. Accordingly, a joint meeting of all stakeholders, including the petitioner and the respondents, shall be convened within a period of one week from today to consider the broader concerns regarding accessibility of films raised by the petitioner," the order said. The Court directed the stakeholders to reach a workable resolution in this regard within two weeks. [ Kamakhya Das v. State of Maharashtra & Ors. ]. Justice Prafulla Khubalkar noted that the electronic devices belonging the accused Kamakhya Das were already seized and custodial interrogation would not be necessary at this stage. Hence, the judge granted bail to Das while asking him cooperate with the ongoing investigation. "Considering the nature of the allegations and the fact that the mobile phone and laptop of the applicant are already seized, at this stage, custodial interrogation need not be insisted upon. Hence, the interim protection granted by the trial court needs to be continued further, subject to certain conditions," the judge held. Das was directed to attend the concerned police station on August 19 and 24 between 10 am to 2 pm. [ Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors] The plea also said there should be criminal action against intermediaries that fail to report CSEAM. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran issued notice to the government on the plea. The Court had also held that an intermediary cannot claim protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 unless it exercises due diligence and complies with its obligations under the POCSO Act and Rules. items.title: Husband called wife barren, wife called husband impotent: What Allahabad HC held
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently observed that addressing a wife as “barren woman” may not constitute cruelty under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) when there is exchange of “filthy verbal blows” from both sides. items.title: Karnataka High Court permits Hindu Jagarana Vedike’s Mysuru torchlight procession on Independence Day eve
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday permitted the Hindu Jagarana Vedike to conduct its ‘Akhanda Bharata Sankalpa Dina’ torchlight procession in Mysuru on the eve of Independence Day [ Hindu Jagrana Vedike & another vs The Commissioner of Police & another ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj , however, made it clear that the procession's organisers would be held responsible if any untoward incident takes place during the march. The Court has directed the police to provide necessary security for the procession from RMC Ganesha Temple to Dodda Gadiyara Circle, which will commence at 5:30 PM and conclude at 7:30 PM on August 14. The Court passed the order after rejecting the State's argument that there is possibility of unlawful incidents arising during the march since some of the programme's organisers had a history of anti-social activities and have criminal cases pending against them. The Court opined that this cannot be a ground to prevent them from participating in Independence Day celebrations. items.title: Supreme Court quashes FIRs against Samay Raina, 4 other comedians over remarks about disabled persons
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashed criminal cases filed against YouTuber-comedian Samay Raina and four other comedians over insensitive remarks made on the show India's Got Latent about persons with disabilities. A Bench Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. Apart from Raina, the others who have been given relief in connection with this case are Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar alias Sonali Aditya Desai, and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The Court today appreciated the efforts made by Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar to organise shows for the benefit of persons with disabilities. " Once there are genuine efforts positive results are bound to be there. They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in positive direction, there will be positive output," the Bench said. The Court proceeded to quash criminal cases filed against them over insensitve remarks against disabled persons.
